title: Taj Hotels in London Serve Diwali Thalis, Brunches and a New Afternoon Tea
excerpt: Taj 51 Buckingham Gate and St. James' Court run a Diwali dining programme from 16 October to 8 November, with thalis at £59, a £56 Quilon brunch and a new Kona afternoon tea from £85.
body:
• Taj 51 Buckingham Gate and St. James' Court in London are running a Diwali dining programme from 16 October to 8 November across five venues.
  • TH@51 serves vegetarian and non-vegetarian thalis at £59 per person, with festive drinks from £16 at TH@51 and 1897 – The Bar.
  • Michelin-starred Quilon offers a £56 vegetarian brunch on 7–8 November, while Bombay Brasserie runs a £61 brunch and a £90 dinner buffet.
  • Kona launches an Indian-inspired afternoon tea on 1 November, Friday to Sunday from £85 — book via the hotels' official dining pages linked below.

London's two Taj hotels have set out a Diwali dining programme that runs for more than three weeks, from 16 October to 8 November, spreading the Festival of Lights across thalis, brunches, buffets and a new afternoon tea rather than a single celebration night. The programme is centred on Taj 51 Buckingham Gate Suites and Residences and St. James' Court, A Taj Hotel, the group's Victorian properties in Westminster near Buckingham Palace, with one venue across town in South Kensington.

Thalis and festive drinks at TH@51

The longest-running element is at TH@51, the hotels' restaurant and bar on Buckingham Gate. From 16 October to 8 November it serves a Diwali thali daily between 12:30pm and 10:30pm at £59 per person, in vegetarian and non-vegetarian versions, according to the programme published by the hotels and reported by Travel PR News. The vegetarian thali includes Kurkuri Bhindi and Aloo Lal Mirchi, while the non-vegetarian version features Macchli Amritsari, Bhuna Gosht and Murgh Butter Masala, finishing with sweets such as Kesari Rasmalai and Gulab Jamun. The £59 price includes a drink, with an additional dessert at £10 and extra portions at £6.

Festive drinks run over the same dates at TH@51 and at 1897 – The Bar, with prices starting at £16, giving visitors a lower-cost way to join the celebrations without booking a full meal. Diners can check menus and opening hours on the restaurant's official TH@51 page, which lists lunch service from 12:30pm and dinner until 10:30pm.

A Diwali weekend at Quilon and Bombay Brasserie

The centrepiece weekend falls on 7 and 8 November. At Quilon, the Michelin-starred restaurant known for the food of India's south-west coast, executive chef Sriram Aylur oversees a vegetarian set brunch served from noon to 3:30pm on both days at £56 per person. The menu opens with a watermelon, lentil, lemon and coconut preparation and moves through Karnataka-style dishes and spiced ghee rice to a broken-wheat kheer, with meat and seafood available separately from an à la carte list that includes pepper shrimps and Goan lamb chop.

Bombay Brasserie in South Kensington takes the opposite approach the same weekend: a buffet. Its Diwali brunch runs from 12:30pm to 3:30pm on 7 and 8 November at £61 per person, or £30 for children aged four to ten, with dishes including paneer pasanda and Hyderabadi-style lamb biryani alongside a live chaat counter. A separate dinner buffet on Saturday 7 November, from 6pm to 10:30pm, is priced at £90 per person.

A new afternoon tea at Kona

From 1 November, Kona introduces an Indian-inspired afternoon tea, pairing regional savouries and spice-led baking with the traditional London format. Sittings run Friday to Sunday at noon and 2pm, from £85 per person. Unlike the one-weekend brunches, the tea is a new standing addition launching during the festival period, extending the programme's life beyond Diwali itself.

What it means for London's diaspora

For London's large Indian community, the programme offers celebration options at several price points within a short distance of each other: a £59 thali available on any day over three weeks, a £56 set brunch, or drinks from £16. Families marking Diwali away from home can book the TH@51 thali or the Kona afternoon tea directly through the hotels' official sites linked above — the Diwali weekend sittings on 7–8 November are the dates most likely to fill first.
